request.task: Certify OBX-AUTH-R1-P1-SOLO-001 inside the complete wave-2 Release 1 governance change
request.head: 226c21b72dd59dc8b04065433a33e6615a523166

findings.scenario: Criterion (2)+(4) require this module to fail closed if implementationAuthorized is true in authority-manifest.json or the program ticket manifest. validateOwnerAcceptance only checks that the release-1 and compatibility domains stay false. Concrete input: set the manifest root implementationAuthorized to true (leave every domain false) and refresh authorityManifestWithoutPacketDigest plus expectedAuthorityWithoutDigestSha256; or set docs/tickets/one-box-program/manifest.json implementationAuthorized to true. Wrong behavior: verifyRelease1PhaseAuthorizations reports no failure for either flag, so a global implementation grant the owner withheld can ride through the named module.
findings.remediation: In validateOwnerAcceptance, fail unless authority.implementationAuthorized === false. Fail if ticketManifest.implementationAuthorized === true. Add node tests that flip each flag by itself and assert the R1 error string.

findings.scenario: Criterion (3)+(4) require P1 governanceBindings and dependencyBindings to be byte-identical to the T02 record, with this module failing closed. The module exact()-compares those arrays to copied constants, not to the live OBX-AUTH-P180-T02-SOLO-001 record. Concrete input: change GOVERNANCE_BINDINGS (or DEPENDENCY_BINDINGS) and the P1 record to a new live file digest while leaving T02's bindings untouched. Wrong behavior: node scripts/verify-r1-phase-authorization.mjs passes even though P1 is no longer identical to T02.
findings.remediation: Load OBX-AUTH-P180-T02-SOLO-001 from the registry and exact() P1 governanceBindings and dependencyBindings to that record's arrays (still live-hash the files). Keep the frozen first-three-records byte pin. Add a test that diverges only the P1 copy.

audit.proof_assessment: No proof artifacts were supplied. Review is static against the diff only. The P1 record shape in scoped-implementation-authorizations.json matches the listed (3) fields (single-file paths, closed effects, empty nonWaivableClassesTouched, null predecessorBinding/activationPrecondition, 336-hour non-renewable window with effectiveExpiresAt 2026-09-14T13:33:33Z sourced from T01, canonical-json-v1 self-hash field). First three registry records are not edited except a trailing comma outside the frozen slice. Manifest top-level and domain implementationAuthorized remain false. Receipts bind the manifest via canonical-json-v1 without /packetDigest, which is the intended stability mechanism for the follow-on re-pin. Hashes themselves were not recomputed here.
residual_risks: Grok receipts are in activationWriteSet/requiredEvidencePaths and the new node tests mutate them, but they are not in this git slice; this review cannot attest they exist or that they only allow the documented T02 targetHashes re-pin.
ownerDirection (record and amendment) is not exact-key-checked; extra keys would pass the module.
validateEffectiveWindow returns without checking the window if either frozen T01/T02 expiresAt is unparsable; the sibling frozen-record check still fails closed in that case.
The R1 module never inspects the T02 security receipt to prove a re-pin changed only four targetHashes digests.
Duplicate JSON key authorizations could desync frozenRegistrySlice (first key) from JSON.parse (last key); ATF/T01/T02 canonical pins in the parent verifier would still need to be beaten.
